# Cycle 1: Code Quality, Profiling & Benchmarking {background-color="#2c3e50"}

## Code Quality Is Part of the Grade

The **Reproducibility & code quality** row of the project rubric is worth 15 points. A grader reading your code looks for:

* **Names that explain themselves:** `life_exp_2019`, not `x2` or `df_final_v3`.
* **One step per line** and consistent spacing, so a pipeline reads top to bottom.
* **Comments that say why**, not what: `# drop territories without population data`.
* **One package chunk** at the top; no dead code, no leftover `View()` or `head()` calls.
* **Labelled chunks** (`#| label: fig-trend`), so errors point to a place.

---

## Before: It Works, But Can You Read It?

```{r}
x<-gm[gm$year==2019&!is.na(gm$continent),];aggregate(x$life_expectancy,list(x$continent),mean,na.rm=T)
```

* Correct numbers, but a reader must decode every symbol.
* `T` can be overwritten (`T <- 0`); always write `TRUE`.

---

## After: The Same Answer, Readable

```{r}
gm |>
  filter(year == 2019, !is.na(continent)) |>        # drop rows with no continent
  group_by(continent) |>
  summarize(mean_life_exp = mean(life_expectancy, na.rm = TRUE))
```

* Same numbers, and each line says what it does.
* Column names describe the result (`mean_life_exp`, not `x`).

---

## Don't Repeat Yourself: Write a Function

```{r}
#| error: true
mean_ci <- function(x, conf = 0.95) {
  if (!is.numeric(x)) stop("`x` must be numeric.")
  if (conf <= 0 || conf >= 1) stop("`conf` must be between 0 and 1.")
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  se <- sd(x) / sqrt(length(x))
  z <- qnorm(1 - (1 - conf) / 2)
  round(c(mean = mean(x), lower = mean(x) - z * se, upper = mean(x) + z * se), 2)
}
rbind(y1999 = mean_ci(gm$life_expectancy[gm$year == 1999]),
      y2019 = mean_ci(gm$life_expectancy[gm$year == 2019]))
mean_ci(gm$continent)
```

---

## Three Ways to Get Daily Counts

Turning **cumulative** counts into daily counts:

```{r}
set.seed(2182)
cumulative <- cumsum(rpois(1000, lambda = 50))   # 1,000 days of cumulative cases

daily_grow <- function(x) {          # grows the result one element at a time
  out <- c()
  for (i in 2:length(x)) out <- c(out, x[i] - x[i - 1])
  out
}
daily_prealloc <- function(x) {      # makes room for the result first
  out <- numeric(length(x) - 1)
  for (i in 2:length(x)) out[i - 1] <- x[i] - x[i - 1]
  out
}
# Third way: the built-in, vectorized diff(cumulative)
```

---

## How Long Does It Take? `system.time()`

```{r}
all.equal(daily_grow(cumulative), diff(cumulative))      # same answer first
all.equal(daily_prealloc(cumulative), diff(cumulative))

system.time(for (k in 1:100) daily_grow(cumulative))     # 100 runs
```

* `elapsed` is wall-clock seconds. One timing is noisy: the next run may differ.

---

## `microbenchmark()`: Compare Precisely

```{r}
set.seed(1)
mb <- microbenchmark(
  grow     = daily_grow(cumulative),
  prealloc = daily_prealloc(cumulative),
  diff     = diff(cumulative),
  times = 100
)
print(mb, unit = "us", signif = 3)
```

```{r}
#| include: false
med <- summary(mb, unit = "us")$median
names(med) <- summary(mb)$expr
```

* Each expression runs 100 times; times are in microseconds (millionths of a second).
* Here `diff()` is about `r round(med[["grow"]] / med[["diff"]])` times faster than growing a vector in a loop.

---

## Seeing the Benchmark

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.2
#| fig-align: center
autoplot(mb)
```

* Log scale: each grid step is a factor of 10. Your timings differ from mine; the **ranking** does not.

---

## Profiling: Find the Slow Step First

```r
# Run in RStudio: profvis opens an interactive viewer, so it cannot run in slides
library(profvis)
profvis({
  states <- readr::read_csv("data/us-states.csv")
  daily  <- daily_grow(states$cases)
})
```

* `profvis` shows how long each line took. Fix the **slowest** line, nothing else.
* For a project report, clear and correct beats fast: optimize only what is actually slow.
* Rule of thumb: **vectorized** functions (`diff()`, `cumsum()`, `mean()`) beat loops; never grow a vector inside a loop.

---

# Cycle 2: Reproducible Repositories for Scientific Audit {background-color="#2c3e50"}

## The Audit Question

> Could someone else **clone your repository** and get **every number** in your report, without asking you anything?

* That is what a journal's reproducibility check does, and what your grader does.
* The rubric asks for a report that **renders from a fresh clone with no errors**.
* A "fresh clone" has only what you committed: no files on your Desktop, no objects in your Environment, no packages loaded by hand.

---

## A Reproducible Project Layout

```{r}
#| echo: false
proj <- file.path(tempdir(), "final-project")
dir.create(file.path(proj, "data"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
invisible(file.create(file.path(proj, c("README.md", "report.qmd", "report.html",
  "final-project.Rproj", ".gitignore", "data/README.md", "data/us-states.csv"))))
```

```{r}
list.files(proj, recursive = TRUE, all.files = TRUE)
```

* `README.md`: who, which data, how to run. `data/README.md`: the data dictionary.
* `report.qmd` plus the rendered `report.html`, committed together.
* `.Rproj` opens RStudio **in this folder**; `.gitignore` keeps clutter out.

---

## Paths: Relative, Never Absolute

| Path | Works on |
|:---|:---|
| `"/Users/maria/Desktop/project/data/us-states.csv"` | Maria's laptop only |
| `"C:/Users/jun/Downloads/us-states.csv"` | Jun's laptop only |
| `"data/us-states.csv"` | Every clone of the repository |

* Quarto renders a report **from the report's own folder**, so `"data/..."` always points inside your repository.
* No `setwd()`: it hard-codes your computer's folders, and Quarto does not need it.

---

## AI Code That Only Works on One Computer

Asked to "load my COVID data and get started," an AI wrote (not run here: it fails on every computer but the author's):

```r
rm(list = ls())                                   # wipes the reader's workspace
setwd("/Users/maria/Desktop/final project")       # Maria's folders only
install.packages("tidyverse")                     # reinstalls on every render
library(tidyverse)
states <- read_csv("C:/Users/maria/Downloads/us-states.csv")
```

* Every line except `library()` breaks reproducibility or someone else's session.
* Install packages **once, in the Console**. Read data with **relative** paths.

---

## Automate the Check

```{r}
check_report <- function(path) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) stop("No file at ", path)
  code <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)
  patterns <- c(setwd = "setwd\\(", install = "install\\.packages\\(",
                rm_all = "rm\\(list", abs_path = "[\"'](/|~|[A-Za-z]:)")
  tibble(problem = names(patterns),
         lines   = map_chr(patterns, \(p) toString(which(grepl(p, code)))))
}
```

* `readLines()` reads the report as text, one element per line.
* `grepl()` flags lines matching each pattern; `which()` gives their line numbers.

---

## Running the Check

```{r}
ai_code <- c('rm(list = ls())', 'setwd("/Users/maria/Desktop/final project")',
             'install.packages("tidyverse")', 'library(tidyverse)',
             'states <- read_csv("C:/Users/maria/Downloads/us-states.csv")')
demo_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".qmd")
writeLines(ai_code, demo_file)

check_report(demo_file)
```

* A hit is a **line to read**, not a verdict: a sentence like "never use `setwd()`" in your prose is flagged too.

---

## Other Reproducibility Habits

* **Seed once**, near the top, before any randomness (Week 10).
* **No hidden state:** restart R before rendering; the report must create every object it uses.
* **Commit the data** your report reads (under 50 MB per file) and the rendered `report.html`.
* **End with `sessionInfo()`** (already in the template): it records R and package versions.
* **Render, then commit, then push**, so `report.html` always matches `report.qmd`.

---

# Cycle 3: Responsible AI Auditing & the AI-Use Appendix {background-color="#2c3e50"}

## Why an AI-Use Appendix?

* AI assistants are **allowed** in the project; every substantive use must be **disclosed**.
* The appendix is worth **15 points**: as much as the video.
* It is graded on **verification**, not on how much or how little AI you used.
* Not using AI is fine: say so, and document how you verified two key results instead.

---

## What Each Entry Records

| Column | What to write |
|:---|:---|
| **Tool** | Which assistant (and version, if you know it). |
| **What I asked** | A summary or the prompt itself. |
| **What I kept or changed** | Which parts you used, edited, or rejected. |
| **How I verified it** | The concrete check, and what it showed. |

Plus at least one entry where the AI was **wrong, incomplete, or needed changes**, with a sentence on what you learned.

---

## Four Ways to Verify

1. **Known value:** run it on a tiny input whose answer you can work out by hand.
2. **Documentation:** read the help page (`?cut`) for the arguments the AI chose.
3. **Second method:** compute the same thing another way and compare.
4. **Edge cases:** boundaries, zeros, `NA`, empty groups, negative numbers.

"It ran without errors" is **not** a verification.

---

## An AI Function to Verify

Asked for "age groups: child under 18, adult 18 to 64, senior 65 and over," an AI wrote:

```{r}
age_group <- function(age) {
  cut(age, breaks = c(0, 18, 65, Inf),
      labels = c("child", "adult", "senior"))
}
age_group(c(5, 40, 80))
```

Three typical ages, three correct labels. Done?

---

## Edge Cases Reveal the Bug

```{r}
test_ages <- c(0, 17, 18, 64, 65)
tibble(age = test_ages, ai_label = age_group(test_ages))
```

* `?cut`: intervals are **closed on the right** by default (`right = TRUE`), so 18 lands in `(0, 18]`.
* Age 0 is outside `(0, 18]` entirely: every newborn becomes `NA`.

---

## A Fix, Checked by a Second Method

```{r}
age_group <- function(age) {
  cut(age, breaks = c(0, 18, 65, Inf), right = FALSE,
      labels = c("child", "adult", "senior"))
}
by_hand <- case_when(test_ages < 18 ~ "child",
                     test_ages < 65 ~ "adult",
                     TRUE ~ "senior")
identical(as.character(age_group(test_ages)), by_hand)
```

* `right = FALSE` makes intervals `[0, 18)`, `[18, 65)`, `[65, Inf)`.
* Two independent methods agree on every boundary.

---

## Weak and Strong Appendix Entries

| | Weak | Strong |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **Asked** | "Help with age groups." | "Code to cut age into child (<18), adult (18–64), senior (65+)." |
| **Kept** | "Used the code." | "Kept `cut()`; added `right = FALSE`." |
| **Verified** | "Checked it, looks right." | "Tested ages 0, 17, 18, 64, 65: the AI version gave `NA` for 0 and put 18 in child. Fixed; matches a `case_when()` version (chunk `check-age`)." |

: {tbl-colwidths="[12,30,58]"}

---

## Make the Verification Visible

```{r}
#| label: check-age
# Verification for AI-use appendix entry 2: boundaries of age_group()
stopifnot(identical(as.character(age_group(c(0, 17, 18, 64, 65))),
                    c("child", "child", "adult", "adult", "senior")))
```

* `stopifnot()` prints nothing when the check passes and **stops the render** if it ever fails.
* Point to the chunk label from your appendix: the grader can see the check, not just read about it.

---

# Cycle 4: Project Workshop + AI Corner {background-color="#2c3e50"}

## AI Corner: The Appendix Entry That Verified Nothing {background-color="#8e44ad"}

A student asked an AI for daily new cases from `us-states.csv`, then asked it to "write my AI-use appendix entry." It produced the code and the entry:

```r
daily <- states |>
  arrange(state, date) |>
  mutate(new_cases = cases - lag(cases))
```

**"How I verified it":** *"I checked `new_cases` against the NYT daily figures for every state; all values were correct and non-negative."*

Sounds thorough. Paste it in?

## AI Corner: Auditing the Claim {background-color="#8e44ad"}

```{r}
states <- tibble(state = rep(c("State A", "State B"), each = 3),
                 date  = rep(as.Date("2020-03-20") + 0:2, 2),
                 cases = c(80, 130, 160, 10, 14, 23))     # toy cumulative counts
states |> arrange(state, date) |> mutate(new_cases = cases - lag(cases))
```

1. No `group_by(state)`: the first day of State B subtracts State A's last count.
2. The NYT files have **no** daily figures to check against, and real revisions make some daily counts negative.
3. Nobody ran the check the entry describes: the AI **wrote a verification it never did**.

## AI Corner: The Audited Version {background-color="#8e44ad"}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
```{r}
daily <- states |>
  arrange(state, date) |>
  group_by(state) |>
  mutate(new_cases = cases - lag(cases)) |>
  ungroup()

# Check: per state, daily counts add up
daily |>
  group_by(state) |>
  summarize(sum_new = sum(new_cases, na.rm = TRUE),
            last_minus_first = last(cases) - first(cases))
```
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
* Group by state, so differences never cross states.
* A check that was **actually run**: daily counts add up to the change in the cumulative count.
* Honest entry: "Rejected the ungrouped version; verified with the sum check in chunk `check-daily`."

::: {.callout-important}
*Never let the AI write the "How I verified it" column. Only you know what you checked.*
:::
:::
:::

---

## Peer Review: How It Works

* Pair up with someone **outside** your usual partner if you can.
* **Round 1 (20 min):** the author shows the draft; the reviewer works through the checklist and records it in the worksheet.
* **Round 2 (20 min):** swap roles.
* The reviewer drives the checklist; the author answers questions but does not defend.
* End each round with **one strength** and **the top three fixes**, each tied to a rubric row.

---

## The Reviewer's Checklist

| Rubric row | Points | Ask |
|:---|---:|:---|
| Introduction | 5 | Can I state the question in one sentence? |
| Packages & data prep | 15 | One package chunk? Source cited? Steps explained? |
| Exploratory analysis | 20 | Labelled figures with units? One point each? |
| Function + simulation/model | 10 | Checked function used twice? Plan for the rest? |
| Summary | 5 | Planned, or already drafted? |
| Reproducibility & code | 15 | Fresh-clone test passes? Inline R for numbers? |
| AI-use appendix | 15 | Each entry has a concrete verification? |

The video (15 points) is not reviewed today.

---

## The Fresh-Clone Test

Run in the **Terminal** (it needs git, so it cannot run in these slides). Copy your repository's URL from the green **Code** button on GitHub:

```bash
cd ~/Desktop
git clone <your-repository-URL> fresh-copy
cd fresh-copy
quarto render report.qmd
```

* Renders here? Then a grader's clone renders too. Fails? Look for a file you never committed or an absolute path.
* Delete `fresh-copy` afterwards so you never edit the wrong folder.

---

## Consultation Clinic

While pairs review, the instructor and CAs circulate. Bring **one specific question**, for example:

* "My figure has 50 overlapping state lines. How do I make one clear point?"
* "Is a bootstrap or a regression the better fit for my question?"
* "My report fails to render on the fresh clone; here is the error."

Questions about your own question, data, or figures are the best use of this time.

---
